overview: CS3101 reintroduces familiarization maneuvers, then moves the student into the IFR environment with an IFR pick-up and GCA pattern. The discussion should show that basic aircraft-control habits, radio discipline, and instrument scan still work when the profile shifts from FAM-style airwork to radar-controlled approaches.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion Items

items.text: Treat the familiarization review as a scan-and-control refresh, not a complete re-teaching of every prior FAM event.

children.text: Be ready to brief G-warm, aerobatics, stalls, spin, unusual-attitude recovery, landing profiles, waveoff, ELP, and holding or approach setup at the level already learned.
For each maneuver, start with purpose, setup, safety boundary, execution, completion cue, and the common error that usually starts the debrief.
Keep checklist, clear-area, trim, coordination, and energy management in every answer.
The sim objective is to rebuild cross-check and aircraft control, then transition smoothly to IFR work.
Do not let the FAM maneuver review consume the IFR brief; prioritize the maneuvers most likely to affect instrument transition, approach work, and recovery judgment.

items.text: An IFR pick-up converts the flight into the IFR system; the radio call must give ATC enough information to identify the aircraft, build the clearance, and understand fuel and alternate context.

children.text: Aircraft identification.
Position and time.
Route, altitude, and destination.
True airspeed in knots.
ETE from the point of change to destination and hours of fuel remaining.
Alternate airport.
Name, rank, and honors code of VIP aboard if the destination is being changed.
Build the call from the current flight state; do not recite a canned local route if the aircraft position, destination, or fuel state has changed.
Keep the aircraft under control and trimmed before starting the clearance conversation.
Read back the clearance precisely and verify route, altitude, transponder, and lost-comm expectations before leaving VFR assumptions behind.

items.text: The GCA pattern is a radar-approach control exercise: fly precise headings, airspeeds, configuration changes, descents, and missed-approach cleanup while the controller or instructor drives small corrections.

children.text: Start clean at 200 KIAS on a cardinal heading at base altitude.
Use standard-rate turns, not more than 30 degrees AOB, and lead rollouts with the one-third rule.
Slow to 150 KIAS using about 15% torque, then stabilize near 33% torque once level at 150 KIAS.
Expect radar-style calls such as standby for the turn, maintain, and clear call when being turned to final approach course.
Transition to BAC by reducing power to about 15%, lowering gear and T/O flaps below 150 KIAS, and executing the Before Landing Checklist.
Trim for 120 KIAS; local event gouge uses about 42% torque to stabilize level at 120 KIAS before the descent.
For the simulated GCA descent, use about 24% torque and a nose-low attitude to hold 120 KIAS and roughly 600 FPM.
Expect small heading corrections, often about 3 to 10 degrees, while maintaining airspeed, descent rate, and assigned headings.
After the planned descent segment, execute the missed approach: maximum power, right rudder, and about 10 to 15 degrees nose high.
Confirm two positive rates with VSI and altimeter before raising the gear.
Above 110 KIAS, raise flaps; report gear and flaps up before 150 KIAS.
Set about 8 to 10 degrees nose high, climb at 180 KIAS for the assigned climb segment, then transition back to 200 KIAS cruise before level-off.
Common errors are poor nose-power coordination in descent, over-rotating during the missed approach, delayed gear or flap retraction, and poor rudder trim causing heading drift.

studyNotes.summary: CS3101 should be studied as a bridge event: refresh FAM maneuver discipline, then use the same aircraft-control habits to execute an IFR pick-up and precise GCA pattern.

summary: CS3101 covers familiarization review, IFR pick-up information, and the GCA pattern profile.
title: IFR Pick-Up
